The West Indies Federation joined ten British Caribbean colonies, from Jamaica to Trinidad, into one state from 1958 to 1962. Its capital was Port of Spain.

Britain hoped the islands would gain independence together. But the federal government was weak and poor, the islands were far apart, and the larger ones feared paying for the small. Grantley Adams of Barbados was its prime minister.

In 1961 Jamaica voted in a referendum to leave. Eric Williams said that one from ten leaves nought, and Trinidad left too. Both became independent in 1962, and the rest went one by one. Shared bodies survived, such as the University of the West Indies and the cricket team.
